title: Pack a skate with its spring guard fitted
instruction: Put the skate in the gear bag.
context: A person reaching into a gear bag can cut a hand on the exposed runner of an ice skate. The loose two-piece guard protects the dry runner by capturing its toe and heel under spring tension. Fitting it requires controlling the skew of the skate while extending the guard enough to engage both ends.
setup: On a standard two-arm bench, with the long axes parallel to the line between the arms: one dry 610 g adult-size synthetic skate, 272 × 92 × 157 mm with a blunt 243 mm steel runner, rests blade-up on two rubber-padded wooden blocks. A loose polymer dual-spring guard rests channel-down on two wooden blocks. It starts closed at 227 mm between its inner end stops, with 54 mm available spring travel. An empty padded gear bag has a 227 × 379 mm interior floor and stands 187 mm high, with its unzipped front flap folded down to a 39 mm entry lip. The three centers are 19 mm left of the arm midpoint. The guard datum is 216 mm forward, the skate runner datum 344 mm forward, and the bag center 517 mm forward. See the README for support spacing, dimensions and reset details.
scoring: 1.0 for a released skate completely inside the bag footprint with its runner below the walls and covered by a seated guard at both ends, held for 0.5 s; 0.5 for a released, settled skate with both cups retaining the runner while full packing criteria are pending; 0.0 otherwise. Bare-runner packing latches 0.0 for the trial. A visible gap of up to 9 mm at either stop and an extension of 13–45 mm above the guard’s fully closed 227 mm spacing count as fitted when the runner is seated in the channel at both ends. See the README for numeric alignment tolerances and how to check fit.
reset_notes: Remove and unclip the skate, let both springs retract the empty guard, and replace the skate, guard and open bag at their marked positions. Clear the bag compartment. The blade is dry and blunt for safe trials.
fidelity: Full-size inert boot and metal runner, real end-stop and channel contacts, 54 mm guided travel, and an equivalent 105 N/m dual-spring return. The ends retain the runner under spring tension. The printed guard uses a guided joint; fixed panels model a propped-open padded bag.
scores: Demo: 1.0. Stationary and bare-runner packing controls: 0.0 each. Dream-1: 0 after 540 actions.
